factual_claims.claim: Konsolidator delivered materially improved financial performance in 2025, although the Group remained loss-making and financially constrained.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Financial Review 2025 section states improved EBITDA loss and operating cash flow but notes consolidated equity remained negative and cash was low.

candidate_sentences.text: Konsolidator delivered materially improved financial performance in 2025, although the Group remained loss-making and financially constrained.

factual_claims.claim: Revenue rose 25% to DKK 25.3m from DKK 20.3m in 2024, driven by subscription revenue increasing from DKK 18.3m to DKK 20.6m and onboarding and consulting fees increasing 134% to DKK 4.7m.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Financial Highlights and Key Figures table shows revenue of DKK 25,282k (2025) vs DKK 20,268k (2024). Periodic Reporting 2025 section confirms subscription fees increased from DKK 9,331k to DKK 10,579k and onboarding/consulting fees from DKK 1,028k to DKK 2,443k.

candidate_sentences.text: Revenue rose 25% to DKK 25.3m from DKK 20.3m in 2024, driven by subscription revenue increasing from DKK 18.3m to DKK 20.6m and onboarding and consulting fees increasing 134% to DKK 4.7m.

factual_claims.claim: The higher onboarding revenue followed price increases for new customers introduced in the first quarter.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Financial Review 2025 states: 'The onboarding and consultancy fees increased by 134%, going from DKK 2.0m in 2024 to DKK 4.7m in 2025. The reason was the increase in onboarding fees as Konsolidator initiated price changes for new customers during Q1 2025.'

candidate_sentences.text: The higher onboarding revenue followed price increases for new customers introduced in the first quarter.

factual_claims.claim: The company ended the year with 283 customers, 52 new customers, and Contracted Annual Recurring Revenue (CARR) of DKK 24.4m, up 15% from DKK 21.3m and above its guidance of DKK 23–24m.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: SaaS Metrics 2025 section states CARR increased by 15% to DKK 24.4m, new customers were 52, and guidance was DKK 23-24m. Market Glance section shows 283 customers at year-end.

candidate_sentences.text: The company ended the year with 283 customers, 52 new customers, and Contracted Annual Recurring Revenue (CARR) of DKK 24.4m, up 15% from DKK 21.3m and above its guidance of DKK 23–24m.

candidate_sentences.text: Average CARR per customer increased from TDKK 70 to TDKK 87.

candidate_sentences.text: The EBITDA loss narrowed to DKK 2.0m from DKK 9.3m, while the net loss declined to DKK 6.6m from DKK 14.9m.

factual_claims.source_evidence: Financial Review 2025 states: 'In 2024, Konsolidator decided to outsource many of the marketing department's activities. The full impact of the outsourcing reduced the EBIT loss by 3m in 2025.' Also notes reduced external expenses.

candidate_sentences.text: The improvement reflected stronger revenue, lower marketing and external costs, and the impact of outsourcing marketing activities, which management states reduced the EBIT loss by DKK 3m.

factual_claims.claim: Other operating income also increased to DKK 2.0m from DKK 0.7m, including income associated with a commercial partner agreement.

candidate_sentences.text: Other operating income also increased to DKK 2.0m from DKK 0.7m, including income associated with a commercial partner agreement.

details.completeness_justification: All key information units are adequately represented in the candidate summary. K1 is covered by S2 (revenue growth), S7 (EBITDA loss improvement), and S10 (H2 positive EBITDA). K2 is covered by S4 (CARR growth), S13 (CAC payback period), and S15 (churn rate). K3 is covered by S17 (product suite expansion). K4 is covered by S4 (new customers), S5 (average customer size), and S18 (partner-driven growth). K5 is covered by S8 (operational efficiency and cost savings). K6 is covered by S20 (equity position) and S21 (private placements). K7 is covered by S22 (2026 guidance). K8 is covered by S19 (Iberia growth). No material omissions affect the overall understanding.

coherence_issues.description: S6 states 'Profitability improved significantly' but S7 and S8 only quantify EBITDA and net loss reductions without defining or measuring profitability. The term remains undefined, creating a logical gap between the claim and supporting evidence.

candidate_sentences.text: Profitability improved significantly.
The EBITDA loss narrowed to DKK 2.0m from DKK 9.3m, while the net loss declined to DKK 6.6m from DKK 14.9m.
The improvement reflected stronger revenue, lower marketing and external costs, and the impact of outsourcing marketing activities, which management states reduced the EBIT loss by DKK 3m.

coherence_issues.description: S12 states the Rule of 40 score increased to 17% from negative 40%, but fails to explain how a negative EBITDA margin (S12: -8%) can produce a positive Rule of 40 score. This creates an unexplained logical disconnect.

candidate_sentences.text: The Rule of 40 score increased to 17% from negative 40%, reflecting 25% revenue growth and an EBITDA margin of negative 8%.

details.coherence_justification: The summary is generally coherent with consistent narrative flow and mostly logical relationships. Key issues are: 1) The profitability claim (S6) lacks definition or quantification, creating a gap between assertion and evidence in S7/S8. 2) The Rule of 40 calculation (S12) appears logically inconsistent with a negative EBITDA margin but is presented without explanation, creating an unexplained gap. No self-contradictions or organizational failures exist. Repetition is minimal and does not materially reduce clarity.
